title: California's 10th Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: The 2026 general election for California's 10th congressional district pits incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative Mark DeSaulnier against Republican small-business owner Jeff Frese. The district covers most of Contra Costa County and a portion of Alameda County in the East Bay. DeSaulnier, first elected in 2014 and a former state senator and assemblymember, is seeking another term on a platform of lowering healthcare and housing costs and protecting Social Security and Medicare. Frese, who advanced by finishing second in the June 2 top-two primary with 12.9% of the vote, is campaigning on affordability, cutting federal regulations, and election integrity. The Cook Political Report rated the general election race as Solidly Democratic before the primary.
polling_note: No general election opinion polls were found for this race as of June 2026. The Cook Political Report rated the race as Solidly Democratic before the primary.

candidates.name: Mark DeSaulnier
candidates.summary: Mark DeSaulnier is the incumbent U.S. Representative for California's 10th congressional district, first elected in 2014. He previously served in the California State Senate (2008–2015), the California State Assembly (2006–2008), and as a Contra Costa County Supervisor (1994–2006). He sits on the House Ethics, Education and Workforce, and Transportation and Infrastructure committees, and his legislative priorities include lowering healthcare and housing costs, protecting Social Security and Medicare, and investing in infrastructure.

candidates.name: Jeff Frese
candidates.summary: Jeff Frese is a Republican candidate and small-business owner from Moraga, California, running for U.S. House in California's 10th congressional district. He advanced to the general election by placing second in the June 2, 2026 top-two primary. His campaign focuses on making California more affordable by cutting federal red tape, reducing wildfire risk through improved forest management, securing elections with voter ID and paper ballots, and implementing term limits for Congress.

forecast.rationale: No general-election polling is available for this race, so the forecast relies entirely on non-polling evidence. Democratic incumbent Mark DeSaulnier has held the seat since 2014 and has extensive prior elected experience at the state and local level. The Cook Political Report rated the contest as Solidly Democratic before the June top-two primary. The district covers most of Contra Costa County and part of Alameda County in the East Bay, a strongly Democratic-leaning area. Republican nominee Jeff Frese advanced with only 12.9% of the primary vote, reflecting the district's partisan composition. Given the absence of direct voter polling, uncertainty remains elevated, supporting a medium confidence level. However, the structural factors point to a safe Democratic hold, consistent with a safe_d rating and a Democratic win probability above 95%.
